summary: Dispatched via codex exec --sandbox read-only -c model_reasoning_effort=high against the first draft's full diff (CodeQL merge_group carry-over + Visa Oracle retry logic). Found: (1) BLOCKER -- the carry-over's premise that a merge_group's analyzed tree is byte-identical to what the PR's own pull_request run analyzed is false (pull_request checks out refs/pull/N/merge, a moving-target test-merge against the base AT TRIGGER TIME; merge_group checks out base-tip + earlier-queued-ahead batchmates + this PR -- these can differ even though the PR's own diff never changed), so carry_over=true could report success without having scanned the merge_group commit; (2) MEDIUM -- exact-name check-run matching has no provenance check (workflow identity, run attempt); (3) MEDIUM -- a step-level timeout-minutes produces outcome=='failure', not 'cancelled' (cited actions/runner's StepsRunner.cs task-result path), so the retry steps gated on outcome=='cancelled' would never fire on an actual timeout; (4) MEDIUM -- the smoke retry's log-grep for the hang signature could match real assertion-failure output containing that substring; (5) MEDIUM -- the same byte-identity premise underlies the merge_group dedup on Snyk/detect-secrets too; (6) LOW -- the SHA regex uses .search() not an anchored full-match.

Dispatched via scripts/tp1_call.py --model qwen3.8-max --effort medium with two targeted technical questions (not a full review): (1) is the carry-over's byte-identical-tree premise actually true, given pull_request's default checkout ref and merge_group's synthetic-ref construction; (2) does a step-level timeout-minutes really report outcome=='cancelled' or 'failure'. Independently confirmed BOTH of codex-gpt-5.6-sol's load-bearing findings with consistent, specific mechanistic detail (refs/pull/N/merge as a moving target; base-tip + earlier-queued-batchmates for merge_group; SIGINT/SIGKILL then TaskResult.Failed, not a cancellation-token path, for step timeout) -- flagged its own confidence as high but not absolute on the second point given no direct empirical test was run this session.

Follow-up review (fresh codex exec dispatch, high effort) against the corrected diff: CodeQL carry-over fully reverted (script deleted, security.yml's codeql job restored to its original three RUN_THIS_LANGUAGE-only conditions, receipt cited: 3 real merge_group runs on 2026-09-04 showing CodeQL's slowest leg at ~15min, well under the 90min queue ceiling); Visa Oracle retry logic reworked to use the POSIX `timeout` utility's own exit code 124 (captured via `set +e` + `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` + explicit `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` write + `exit "$rc"` re-raise), never GitHub Actions' step outcome, for hang detection. Confirmed both direct questions YES (CodeQL blocker fully resolved; retry logic no longer depends on the disproven outcome=='cancelled' assumption, and the set+e/PIPESTATUS/exit-code mechanics are correct) but raised a NEW BLOCKER: the same false byte-identical-tree premise was still present, unchanged, in the merge_group dedup comments on snyk-python/snyk-node/snyk-docker/detect-secrets from item 1 of this PR -- and for snyk-docker specifically, cited a real, pre-existing, DOCUMENTED incident in this exact file (run 30302472020, a merge_group run that caught a broken Docker build the PR-head run had missed) as direct historical proof the premise fails for that job. Also raised: MEDIUM -- timeout without --kill-after can hang past its own nominal budget if the wrapped process ignores SIGTERM; LOW -- ${PIPESTATUS[0]} in the smoke step's tee pipe doesn't capture tee's own exit status; LOW -- snyk-python's new comment named the wrong file (requirements.lock.txt/uv.lock instead of the job's real target, requirements.txt, contradicting the job's own pre-existing comment one line above it).

Dispatched via scripts/tp1_call.py --model qwen3.8-max --effort medium to arbitrate a specific disagreement: after independently verifying codex-gpt-5.6-sol's snyk-docker finding (confirmed via direct grep of the file's own pre-existing comment citing run 30302472020) was correct and reverting ONLY snyk-docker (not all four flagged jobs), asked whether the partial revert was defensible or whether snyk-python/snyk-node/detect-secrets also needed a full revert. Verdict AGREE: the line drawn (compositional build risk on snyk-docker, which builds an image whose two-PR-interaction failure mode is structurally real, vs. a per-item CVE/pattern lookup on the other three, which is not compositionally sensitive to a batchmate's unrelated change) is the correct line. Tried to construct concrete non-contrived counter-scenarios for each of the three surviving skips (dependency-resolution interaction, overrides/resolutions field abuse, baseline-suppression-removal-plus-secret-addition, cross-file secret construction) and found none survive as realistic, given each job's advisory-only status and each job's per-item (not compositional) analysis model. One suggested polish (non-blocking): make the advisory-only dependency machine-greppable via an explicit 'if this job is ever made required, remove the merge_group skip' comment -- applied to snyk-python's and detect-secrets' comments (snyk-node references snyk-python's rationale by pointer, so it inherits the note).
